title: Stability orchestrator for graded tripping and safe fallback fanout
creator: Sofia Chen
description: Motivation: We need a unified orchestrator that implements graded circuit-tripping across dimensions (dependency health, model quality regressions, per-tenant stability) and executes safe fallback fanout rules. Current per-path breakers are brittle: they either fully cut traffic or stay permissive. The orchestrator will: 1) evaluate multi-signal trip scores (latency p50/p95/p99, error-rate, quality regressions tied to eval prompts), 2) compute a graded trip level per dependency/model/tenant, 3) select a safe fallback fanout (e.g., local cache, quantized model, regional replica, or synthetic empty response) with a ranked preference and cost/quality estimate, 4) expose explainable trip rationale to Console and tracing, and 5) provide canary dry-run and staged rollout controls.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Orchestrator returns a trip-level (0-3) and fallback candidates for a simulated load profile in staging for each dependency & model
2) Default policy degrades gracefully: level 1 -> reduced qps, level 2 -> regional reroute with rate cap, level 3 -> safe synthetic/cached fallback
3) Traces and Console show trip rationale fields (signals used, weights, timestamp) for at least 90% of tripped requests in staging
4) Load test: under a controlled 30% extra latency injected into europe region, 80% of tenants routed to fallback according to policy within SLA without cascading failures
5) Automated canary: deployment can be toggled to dry-run mode and produce identical trip decisions without affecting production traffic
6) Playbook documented and runbook validated by SRE and Support with <30m mean mitigation time in tabletop exercise
design_notes: Signal inputs: p50/p95/p99 latency, error-rate (5xx/timeout), model-quality drift score (eval set A/B mismatch), region capacity headroom, per-tenant rate quota remaining
Trip scoring: each signal normalized to [0,1], apply configurable weights per dependency type, combine with a sigmoid mapping to discrete trip levels (0-none,1-caution,2-limited,3-cutover)

Fallback ranking: (1) prefix KV cached response, (2) local quantized model (lower-cost, lower-quality), (3) regional replica in lower-cost region, (4) simplified deterministic path (templated reply), (5) hard deny with informative error. Each candidate has expected quality loss and cost delta metadata
Policy primitives: per-tenant budget (qps & percent), tenant-priority overrides, model-affinity tags to prefer same-family fallbacks
Observability: enrich spans with 'trip.score', 'trip.signals', 'fallback.reason', and emit event to metrics pipeline for histogram of trip levels per-tenant/model/region
Safety: require two independent signals to trigger level 3; any level 3 fallback must have an automated rollback timer and be recorded in incident-log
Explainability: store top-3 contributing signals and weights with each trip event to allow audit and postmortem reasoning
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (dry-run staging): deploy orchestrator with dry-run=true for all staging tenants, collect trip events and adjust weights (2 weeks)
Phase 1 (canary): enable orchestrator for 2% of production traffic with strict throttles and monitoring (3 days)
Phase 2 (regional ramp): enable in single non-critical region (EU-west) with level-3 disabled, verify no user-facing errors (1 week)
Phase 3 (full-enforcement): enable globally with throttles and auto-rollback policies in place (monitor for 1 week), then tune defaults
Rollback criteria: >1% increase in 5xxs or >2x latency regression at p99 for operator-facing routes within 15 minutes -> automatic rollback to previous policy
testing_plan: Unit tests for score normalization and threshold mapping (coverage >90%)
Integration tests: simulated signal injection harness that verifies fallback selection across 500 synthetic tenants
Chaos tests: region latency-injection and replica loss scenarios in staging using Chaos Toolkit
Load tests: run 2000 rps mixed workload with staging replica set and verify failover percentages match expected policy within +/-5%
Canary monitor checklist: dashboards for trip-rate, fallback-type distribution, tenant-regressions, and false-positive rate
metrics: metric.trip_false_positive_rate : fraction of trips reversed by dry-run signals
customer-impact incidents correlated with trip events
decision_log: 2025-11-10: Chose discrete levels (0-3) over continuous percentage shedding to simplify rollout and SLAs (agreed with PM & SRE)
2025-11-17: Default fallback ranking decided to prefer local cache then quantized model to minimize cross-region egress costs
2025-11-24: Require two independent signals to escalate to level 3 to avoid noisy full cutovers
2025-11-28: Added explainability fields to event schema after privacy review to ensure no PII is included
comments: 2025-11-05 Sofia Chen: Initial ticket created after incident retro revealed brittle per-dep breakers. Attached design doc draft.
2025-11-12 Priya Patel (PM): Reviewed weighting proposal; requested tenant-priority override and clear operator controls for enterprise customers.
2025-11-18 Marcus Rivera: Implemented core scoring function and added unit tests. Opened PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1284
2025-11-20 SRE Team (Alex Wong): Ran staging dry-run; observed high trip-rate for low-traffic tenants due to aggressive normalization. Suggested percentile-based floor per-tenant.
2025-11-25 Design review: Agreed to expose top-3 signals in Console and add a toggle to hide signals for tenants with strict data policies.
2025-11-30 Load test: injected 200ms extra p95 in EU-west — orchestrator routed 78% of affected traffic to quantized local models; no customer-facing errors observed. Docs and dashboards updated.
2025-12-02 Marcus Rivera: PR merged to staging; requesting final review for production rollout. Noted one follow-up to add synthetic response templates for edge-case fallbacks.
